author: Maanvi Singh and agencies
description:
According to manufacturer, shock ‘is usually effective in bringing individuals into compliance in less than three seconds’

ICE plans to spend up to $20m (£15m) to purchase thousands of gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks for officers and agents by March, according to a notice published Monday by the Department of Homeland Security.

The devices, called Glove (Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter), are manufactured by Compliant Technologies LLC of Lexington, Kentucky.

Continue reading...
title: ICE to spend up to $20m on gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Policy comes as debate continues over causes of and solutions to housing issues. Follow today’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Education minister says funding agreement with Victoria ‘very close’

The education minister, Jason Clare, says a funding deal with Victoria to get public schools funded to Gonski levels over the next decade is “very close”.

We’re very close, mate. I know [Victorian premier] Ben Carroll gets this and I’m optimistic that we’ll get this across the line. He understands how important it is that teachers are paid well, that they do the best or do the most important job in the country, but how important it is that we fix the funding
title: Australia politics live: Coalition to heavily cut net migration and shred 96% of house construction code; CBA posts bumper $11bn profit

author: Reuters
description:
Ruling expands on earlier order that prevented implementation in 23 mostly Democratic-led states

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A federal judge on Tuesday blocked ⁠the US Postal ⁠Service ​(USPS) from implementing part of Donald Trump’s executive order that aims ⁠to tighten rules for mail-in voting ahead of November midterm elections that ⁠will decide control of Congress.

The ruling by ​US district ‌judge Indira ‌Talwani in Boston in effect expanded on an ‌earlier order she had issued in June that had prevented Trump’s administration from implementing it in 23 mostly Democratic-led states.
title: Judge blocks Trump’s order aimed at using USPS to restrict mail-in voting

author: Guardian staff
description:
Reform deputy leader condemned for seeking disclosure of documents that could reveal reporter’s sources

Richard Tice has been accused of using “nasty tactics” in an attempt to intimidate journalists and deflect attention from his own financial affairs after issuing a legal threat to the Guardian.

In a letter sent from his lawyers, a Guardian correspondent was singled out for her reporting on a series of Tice’s financial transactions that were referred to the National Crime Agency.

Continue reading...
title: Richard Tice accused of ‘nasty tactics’ over legal threat to the Guardian

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Star, 53, says disease has metastasised to her bones and it is too late for chemotherapy

Lucy Davis, the actor best known for playing Dawn Tinsley in The Office, has said she has incurable stage four breast cancer.

The 53-year-old said she was diagnosed a year and a half ago and the disease had metastasised to her bones including her spine, right hip and ribs. She said it was too late for chemotherapy.

Continue reading...
title: The Office actor Lucy Davis says she has incurable stage four breast cancer

author: Nadeem Badshah
description:
Clifford Wilby, 63, blocked the Walthamstow MP from leaving, filmed her and talked about her ‘failings as a member of parliament’

A 63-year-old man has been found guilty of harassing the Labour MP Stella Creasy after he was “abusive and aggressive” to her on a tube train.

Clifford Wilby, of east London, saw the MP for Walthamstow in July 2025 on a Victoria Line train, Westminster magistrates court heard.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Abusive’ man found guilty of harassing Stella Creasy MP on tube train

author: Dharna Noor
description:
Critics argue US high court justice should recuse himself from upcoming fossil fuel firms’ climate accountability case

Supreme court justice Samuel Alito gained up to $2.9m from his fossil fuel interests between 2005 and 2024, a new review of financial disclosures shows.

The analysis from the non-profit advocacy group and judicial watchdog Court Accountability, shared exclusively with the Guardian, found that even at the lowest range of estimates, Alito gained almost $400,000 from his oil and gas interests since being tapped for the high court by George W Bush in 2005.

Continue reading...
title: Samuel Alito gained up to $2.9m from oil and gas assets since joining supreme court, analysis shows

author: Sandra Laville in the New Forest
description:
Key tourist route closed and residents rallying round as battle against wildfire expected to go on for several days

The battle to contain a large wildfire spreading across the New Forest will go on for several days, experts have said, as wind changes and a desiccated landscape fuel the flames.

Smoke billowed above the deserted A31 road, the main tourist route into the New Forest national park where tens of thousands of families are on holiday, late on Tuesday while a helicopter flew above the blaze. Firefighters at the scene said they were trying to contain several hotspots across the more than 100 hectares (247 acres) of dried heathland as winds swirled over the area.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Real struggle’ to tame New Forest blaze as UK set for hottest summer on record

author: Coral Murphy Marcos
description:
Jacob ‘Jake’ Whisenant died in Sequoia and Kings Canyon wilderness in ‘climbing-related incident’, authorities say

A 30-year-old California climber known for breaking speed records died after falling in the Sierra Nevada wilderness last week, according to authorities.

Jacob “Jake” Whisenant, from Mammoth Lakes, California, died in the Sequoia and Kings Canyon wilderness on 3 August, according to the Tulare County sheriff’s office coroner unit and the National Park Service (NPS).

Continue reading...
title: Record-breaking El Capitan climber dies in Sierra Nevada fall

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Revocations targeted foreign nationals who allegedly broke terms of their visas, says Department of State

The US Department of State has canceled more than 175,000 visas since Donald Trump returned to office, quadrupling the pace of revocations under Joe Biden’s final year in the White House, according to a new tally released by the department this week.

The announcement said the revocations targeted foreign nationals who allegedly broke the terms of their visas, committed crimes, called for violence against Americans, defrauded US citizens, abused the immigration system or endangered national security. Many followed run-ins with law enforcement, the department said, with assault, drunk driving, theft and drug offenses the leading causes, alongside reckless driving, sexual assault, child abuse and fraud.

Continue reading...
title: US state department has canceled over 175,000 visas since Trump’s return to office

author: Daisy Ayliffe
description:
Prof Wyn Evans, who raised concerns over treatment of female staff at Institute of Astronomy, was subject to ‘baseless’ investigation, judge rules

A University of Cambridge whistleblower who alleged bullying of female staff inside the university’s Institute of Astronomy has won a tribunal against his employer.

Prof Wyn Evans told a tribunal hearing in June that the institute suffered from “a bad history of misogyny”. He claimed that one woman in the department had been “hounded out of a job”, another was “left a frightened woman”, and a third had faced “aggressive professors” at the institute.

Continue reading...
title: University of Cambridge whistleblower who reported alleged bullying wins employment tribunal

author: Alice Speri
description:
Lawsuit challenges executive order targeting international criminal court for investigating Israeli crimes in Palestine

Four prominent US human rights organizations have accused the Trump administration of using its “crippling” sanctions regime against the international criminal court (ICC) to undermine global efforts to prosecute war crimes and crimes against humanity.

In a lawsuit filed in federal court on Tuesday, the groups – the American Friends Service Committee, the Center for Constitutional Rights, Human Rights Watch and the Open Society Institute – argued that the administration’s targeting of the ICC, as well as of groups and individuals affiliated with it or assisting its work, amounts to a “blatantly illegal attack on international justice”, the groups said.
title: Human rights groups sue Trump administration over ‘crippling’ ICC sanctions

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
When it comes to the Reserve Bank, there’s a whiff of a parent making a threat they have no intention of carrying out

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Every parent makes threats in an effort to get their kids to behave – and every parent hopes they won’t have to follow through.

Some (most?) parents even make threats they have zero intention of carrying out.

Continue reading...
title: The RBA likely believes it won’t need to hike rates again – but the worst thing it could do is say that out loud

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Angus Taylor and Matt Canavan will support Pauline Hanson’s migration bill despite vowing to fight her rightwing party

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Coalition will back a plan by Pauline Hanson to prevent Australian citizens with links to overseas terrorist groups from returning home, significantly elevating One Nation’s policy prescriptions on matters of national security.

Despite pledging to fight Hanson’s insurgent rightwing movement amid collapsing support for their own parties, the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, and Nationals leader, Matt Canav
title: Coalition to back One Nation policy barring overseas Australians with terrorist links from returning home

author: Olivia Bowden in Toronto
description:
Flight from Victoria to Toronto forced to return to terminal after repeated attempts to secure child in seat failed

A Canadian airline cancelled a flight from Victoria to Toronto after a child refused to wear a seatbelt.

The child was standing in their chair as the 6 August Porter Airlines flight taxied towards the runway, the airline said. Repeated attempts by an accompanying parent and crew to secure the child in their seat failed, so the crew elected to return to the terminal and have the two passengers disembark as “the aircraft could not take off in this unsafe condition”, it added.

Continue reading...
title: Canadian airline cancels flight after child refuses to wear seatbelt

author: Phillip Inman
description:
The new PM could bring in revenue for social care or defence with a land levy or by reforming council tax

Residential property is the largest store of wealth in the UK, and has long been a target for those who believe homes should be taxed more. Real estate remains a juicy plum for Andy Burnham to pick as he searches for ways to pay for an overhaul of the social care system and higher defence spending, to name just two fiscal priorities. Yet how to tax property, or possibly the land it sits on, has vexed economists and politicians for centuries. Here we discuss the background to the debate and some of the tax options.

Continue reading...
title: Axe stamp duty? How Andy Burnham could change property tax

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Poll finds consensus on what makes people proud to be British but deep divisions on issues such as immigration

You may think it’s a commitment to buying a round, the ability to chat at length about the weather, or making a proper cup of tea. But when it comes down to what makes people proud to be British, there is a consensus across all ages, demographics and political groups – and tea, pints and the weather don’t get a look-in.

Hard work, fair play and community are the values that voters – no matter which political party, age group, social class or region they come from – instinctively believe capture what it means to be British, according to a large-scale study of British values by Public First.

Continue reading...
title: Hard work or humour? Take the British values quiz

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Baltimore officer Dequwan Houchins, 30, indicted for allegedly making false traffic stop reports for months

A Baltimore, Maryland, police officer avoided service calls by claiming he was on traffic stops when he was in fact “sitting idle in his car”, according to an indictment filed by city prosecutors.

Dequwan Houchins, 30, is accused of four counts of false entry in a public record and five counts of misconduct in office and could face 12 years in jail and a $4,000 fine for each of the false entry charges, if convicted.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A lazy cop’: Maryland police officer allegedly faked traffic stops to avoid service calls

author: Martin Belam
description:
Buildings collapse and more than 470 people hurt in 7.4-magnitude quake. Plus, in such a vast universe why is there no sign of aliens?

Good morning. More than 130 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in main cities, including Cali and Pereira.

The US and Colombian geological surveys reported that a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck at 7.34am local time on Monday, with its epicentre in the western department of Chocó. It was felt in neighbouring Venezuela, still reeling from a deadly double earthquake on 24 June. The quake killed at least 132 people and more than 570 were injured as of Monday afternoon, according to the Colombian Association of Capital Cities, which coordinates cities across the country.

How has the government responded? In a national addre
title: Colombia reels after major earthquake kills at least 130 | First Thing

author: Steven Morris
description:
Staff at North Devon district hospital given training in difficult births in case mothers-to-be cannot get to Exeter

Doctors at one of England’s remotest hospitals have been given a “crash course” in birth emergencies after its maternity unit was shut and as fears grow that the safety of women and babies may be put at risk.

From Tuesday, the maternity service at North Devon district hospital (NDDH) in Barnstaple has been suspended indefinitely owing to staff shortages, leaving many pregnant women facing a journey of at least an hour and a half when they go into labour.

Continue reading...
title: Doctors at remote Devon hospital get ‘crash course’ after maternity unit shut

On the left, Peggy Flanagan, the state lieutenant governor and a progressive, faces off against Angie Craig, a US representative, for the Democratic bid for US senate in a race punctuated by the role of immigration enforcement in the state that saw two resid
title: Democratic progressives and establishment set to clash in more primaries – US politics live

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Largest for-profit hospital system and operator in the US reported $6.8bn in profits, while employees find it difficult to make ends meet

Union workers with HCA Healthcare, the largest for-profit hospital system and operator in the US, are holding picket protests across the country as they push for pay and staffing increases in a new contract.

The hospital system has over 300,000 employees in the US and the UK, with 22,000 US workers represented by the Service Employees International Union (SEIU) who are in contract negotiations with HCA. Workers are asking for a pathway to a $25 an hour minimum wage, improved wage scales and raises that match the increased cost of living, along with benefits including paid vacation, sick time and bolstered work protections.
title: HCA workers push for higher pay and more staffing amid billions in profits: ‘I’m struggling’

author: Jason Wilson
description:
Two advisers have links to a venture fund co-investing in US defense companies that benefit from federal spending

Pete Hegseth’s appointments to a key Pentagon advisory body include two men with ties to the venture capital fund where Donald Trump Jr is a partner, which has lucrative investments in military and space technology.

Defense Policy Board appointee Marc Andreessen’s firm, Andreessen Horowitz, one of Silicon Valley’s largest venture capital firms and known by the name “a16z”, co-invests alongside the Trump partnership 1789 Capital in three defense contractors. Fellow DPB appointee Blake Masters also sits on the boards of three ventures tied to 1789 Capital.

Continue reading...
title: Pete Hegseth’s Pentagon picks raise questions over Trump family business ties

author: Kalyeena Makortoff
description:
Rooms in Icelandic capital Reykjavík cost double usual rate and Spain also enjoying strong bookings

  • Europe’s total solar eclipse: the best place to see it

Hotel prices have surged in key European cities as hundreds of thousands of tourists flock to see the first total eclipse visible from the continent this century.

Iceland’s capital, Reykjavík, has seen one of the biggest jumps in hotel room prices, being one of the few accessible locations to see the full eclipse before evening on Wednesday.

Continue reading...
title: Hotel prices in Europe jump before total solar eclipse

author: Matthew Weaver
description:
Exclusive: Court service says anyone trying to enter buildings with glasses will have them confiscated and returned when they leave

Courts in England and Wales have joined a number of restaurants, theatres and pubs in banning Meta glasses, amid a mounting backlash against what has been described as “spyware”.

Last month courts in New York announced a ban on the controversial glasses, which can record video footage while being worn.

Continue reading...
title: Meta glasses banned from courts in England and Wales

author: George Chidi
description:
Republicans, including Graham’s sister Darline, expedite campaigns to replace late senator in special primary race

In the race to replace the late US senator Lindsey Graham, 10 candidates have been barnstorming South Carolina diners, church halls and recreation centers, compressing a normal year of campaigning into about a fortnight.

The Republican party is staging a special primary election in the state on Tuesday to choose Graham’s replacement. His sister, Darline, who has been serving as interim senator following his sudden death last month, is on the ballot.

Continue
title: ‘Fiercely independent’ South Carolina votes on Lindsey Graham’s Senate successor

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
From progressive and moderate to election deniers, state sees wide spectrum of candidates in test of direction for both parties

Minnesota voters on both sides of the aisle are weighing the direction of their parties – and their chances of winning over the general electorate – in marquee statewide races on Tuesday.

On the left, Peggy Flanagan, the state lieutenant governor and a progressive, faces off against Angie Craig, a US representative, for the Democratic bid for US senate in a race punctuated by the role of immigration enforcement in the state that saw two residents killed by immigration agents in a winter surge.

Continue reading...
title: Minnesota primaries could mark change of path for Democrats and Republicans

author: Victoria Bekiempis in New York
description:
Prosecutors allege 28-year-old gunned down Brian Thompson outside Manhattan hotel in 2024

Luigi Mangione, who is accused of the killing of the UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, is due to appear on Tuesday morning at Manhattan state court.

Mangione’s appearance comes less than a month before the start of his highly anticipated 8 September trial. Prosecutors allege that Mangione gunned down Thompson outside a Midtown Manhattan hotel on 4 December 2024.

Continue reading...
title: Luigi Mangione due to appear in New York court over healthcare CEO’s killing

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Analysis finds nearly one in six people leaving jail last year in England and Wales were released into homelessness

Andy Burnham’s pledge to end rough sleeping is under threat from a failure to find accommodation for a growing number of newly released prisoners, a charity has warned.

An analysis by the social justice charity Nacro has found that nearly one in six people leaving jail in England and Wales last year were released into homelessness, reaching the highest rate for five years.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham rough-sleeper pledge at risk from failures in housing ex-prisoners, charity warns

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Burnham has asked the justice secretary Alex Norris to come to parliament in September with solution

Aileen O’Connor, chair of the Police Federation in Thames Valley, where PC Andrew Harper was an officer, has welcomed the news that Andy Burnham has ordered another rethink on the prisoner early release scheme.

She told the Today programme this morning:

There’s a little bit of glimmer of hope and encouragement with this latest release that we heard last night, but I can’t lose sight of just hours before that we heard that there was no possibility. So for me, I’m encouraged, I’m optimistic.

And I genuinely believe that the powers that be, Andy Burnham – and the difficult decisions that they have to make – he will make the right choices here, and he will come on board with us, and he’ll get the right side of the line.
title: Rayner says Burnham won’t accept ‘system says no’ advice over prisoner release scheme – UK politics live

author: Yohannes Lowe
description:
Amber heat health alerts are now in effect across all regions of England, aside from the north east

Farmers have reported their earliest harvests in 20 years, with reduced yields, while reservoir levels have fallen to 69% – 11.6% lower than expected for this time of year.

Paul Tompkins, the deputy president of the National Farmers’ Union, said that with no meaningful rain forecast in the coming weeks, the situation for farmers was increasingly concerning. He said:

Many farmers have completed the earliest harvest on record, with poor yields in key crops reported in some areas of the country.

Livestock and dairy farmers are already using winter feed because grass has stopped growing, while growers are working hard to keep fruit and vegetables watered, but many are struggling to access the water they need.
title: Amber heat health alerts kick in across most of England ahead of fifth summer heatwave – latest news

author: Catie McLeod Consumer affairs reporter
description:
Fair Work Commission issues a new minimum standards order for gig workers to come into effect 17 August

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Delivery drivers in Australia will be paid a minimum rate of $31.30 an hour and insured for injuries on the job under a landmark agreement approved by the industrial umpire.

The Fair Work Commission (FWC) on Tuesday issued a new minimum standards order for gig workers who perform on-demand delivery of food, drinks, or groceries, and the operators of the digital platforms who engage their services.

Continue reading...
title: Delivery drivers to be paid minimum $31.30 an hour across Australia in ‘world-leading’ decision

author: PA Media
description:
West London airport reports 7.86 million passengers in July, compared with 8.15 million for Istanbul

  • Business live – latest updates

Heathrow airport has argued “the case for expansion has never been clearer” after it lost its position as Europe’s busiest airport to Istanbul.

Figures published on Tuesday showed 7.86 million passengers passed through Heathrow’s four terminals in July,whereas its Turkish counterpart recorded 8.15 million passengers over the same period.

Continue reading...
title: Heathrow says need for expansion ‘clear’ as it loses title of Europe’s busiest airport

author: Caroline Davies
description:
Andy Burnham said to be ‘determined’ to work out solution amid increasing pressure from family and police

Andy Burnham has told the justice secretary to find a way to exclude PC Andrew Harper’s killers from the early release scheme aimed at easing prison overcrowding.

The prime minister is said to be “determined” to find a solution amid increasing pressure from Harper’s family and police not to allow Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter, to be freed in January under the existing plans.

Continue reading...
title: PM asks justice secretary to find way to exclude PC Harper’s killers from early release scheme

author: Josh Butler
description:
Anthony Albanese faces criticism after appearing to joke on a podcast about a gift of melons from Sanae Takaichi

The Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has rejected calls to apologise to Japan’s prime minister over a joke he made about melons on a satirical podcast, amid a media frenzy and accusations of sexual innuendo.

Government MPs have defended the prime minister as criticism mounted over last month’s remarks, branded by the Coalition opposition as “grubby”. The assistant minister Pat Gorman told media: “I don’t know why we’re still talking about this.”

Continue reading...
title: Australia’s prime minister refuses to apologise to Japanese counterpart over melon gaffe

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Barclays says survey shows people feel more secure in jobs and have more leeway to spend on non-essentials

  • Business live – latest updates

Consumer confidence hit its highest level in almost two years in July, according to research that indicated the closing stages of the men’s football World Cup and more people holidaying in the UK lifted summer spending.

A truce in the Middle East conflict in June and the arrival of a new prime minister in No 10 also gave a lift to consumers after a long period of heightened uncertainty.

Continue reading...
title: Consumer confidence at near two-year high as World Cup and UK holidaying lift summer spending

author: Josh Butler and Tom McIlroy
description:
Some Liberal and National MPs warned against over-regulation in party room discussion, while others argued for more stringent rules

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Coalition MPs have warned the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, not to overreach in talks with Anthony Albanese on Labor’s gambling adv
title: Coalition divided over tougher gambling laws - with MPs warning Angus Taylor against overreach

author: Michael Segalov
description:
In today’s newsletter: As we enter our fifth summer heatwave, Andy Burnham’s government is looking at what the UK should do with its remaining North Sea oil and gas

Good morning. What a difference a new job can make. “To have a shot at staying within 1.5C global warming, we can’t have any new oil or gasfields … It’s irresponsible and shortsighted to be funding new #fossilfuels when we need to be getting to #NetZero.”

This was the 2022 message from Miatta Fahnbulleh, now the secretary of state for energy security and net zero. It’s a testament to her remarkable rise that Fahnbulleh wasn’t even an MP when she posted it four years ago. Today, she is in the cabinet, facing (or is the face of, at least) one of the most challenging, and potentially controversial questions looming for the new government: to drill or not to drill, baby?

Two sites are the focus of fierce debate. Yesterday, a public consultation on whether to greenlight extraction at one of them – Jackda
title: Tuesday briefing: To drill or not to drill – Burnham’s first big climate test

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Consultant Jeremy Greenwood gives evidence to Independent Commission Against Corruption as it investigates allegations linked to Christian Liberal group

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former lobbying firm which allegedly accepted illegal donations to fund factional Liberal party work created a fake administrative assistant called “Jessica”, an inquiry has heard.

Consultant and lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood gave his second day of evidence to
title: Lobbying firm linked to Reformers created fake administrative assistant named ‘Jessica’, Icac hears

author: Luca Ittimani and Patrick Commins
description:
In a widely expected decision, the Reserve Bank of Australia holds interest rate after three hikes earlier this year

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Reserve Bank has held the official cash rate at 4.35% but threatened to hike again if needed, as it warned falling house prices will slow income growth.

The widely expected decision comes after a steep decline in property values in Sydney and Melbourne arrived in Brisbane, Perth and Adelaid
title: RBA interest rates: Reserve Bank holds cash rate at 4.35% but threatens more hikes if needed

author: Josh Halliday
description:
Parent-carers of disabled children are exposed to chronic levels of extreme stress and often reach crisis point before help is available – then they face a ‘fight for basic support’, experts say. This is Matilda Davis’s story

Two days before she died, Matilda Davis issued a plea on Facebook. Sharing a study that found more than 40% of parent-carers had considered suicide, she called for “greater awareness, action and change” in Britain’s broken social care system. “This speaks the words I can’t,” she wrote.

Matilda, known as Tilly to her family and friends, had spent years battling for support in a regime that close observers and those who rely on it often say is increasingly confusing, fragmented and difficult to navigate.

Continue reading...
title: Matilda in pieces: what one mother’s suicide reveals about the carers broken by the system

author: Nimra Shahid and Damien Gayle
description:
Supply in nine blocks in Tower Hamlets affected with some residents suspecting nearby building developments

  • They cannot even flush their toilets: life in east London blocks where taps often run dry

Hundreds of residents in blocks of flats in east London have been left without regular running water for more than seven months after development in the area may have left it without an adequate supply.

Taps have been running dry in nine blocks in Tower Hamlets, where residents have been forced to use bottled water while their landlord, the housing association Poplar Harca, delayed works to solve the problem.

Continue reading...
title: Hundreds in London flats left without regular running water since last year

author: Amanda Meade
description:

An alleged victim of Alan Jones told his older brother, after the broadcaster was arrested, that his indecent assaults weren’t “too bad” but involved Jones grabbing his penis, a Sydney court has heard.

The witness on Tuesday was asked by the trial prosecutor Georgina Wright to descr
title: Alan Jones trial: alleged victim told brother indecent assaults weren’t ‘too bad’ but involved broadcaster grabbing his penis, court hears

Lord mayor says Town Hall square will be ‘fantastic’ – but business advocate says project’s scale of demolition presents ‘unwanted disruption’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Sydneysiders have been given a first glimpse of a new public square set to “unify” the CBD, more 40 years after the project was initially conceived.

The City of Sydney on Tuesday released new renders of a plaza that will be built opposite Sydney town hall after the cou
title: Clover Moore unveils 4,500 sq metre Sydney plaza design after more than 40 years of planning

author: Lisa Cox
description:
Federal government also hopes to vaccinate some wild birds but admits catching them once, let alone twice for both doses, is ‘difficult’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Vaccinations against H5 bird flu will be rolled out for Australian native bird species in captivity as the deadly virus continues to spread across the country.

The federal agriculture minister, Julie Collins, said on Tuesday that target native species in captivity would be prioritised with the first vaccinations to commence “in the coming days and weeks”.

Continue reading...
title: Native birds in captivity to be vaccinated against H5 bird flu as Australia prepares for more mass mortalities

author: Chris Stein in Asheville, North Carolina
description:
Jennifer Balkcom to face Democrat Jamie Ager in race to represent North Carolina’s 11th congressional district

North Carolina Republicans on Monday chose state lawmaker Jennifer Balkcom to replace Chuck Edwards, the incumbent congressman who earlier this month dropped his re-election bid after a US House investigation determined his conduct towards to young female staffers likely amounted to sexual harassment.

Balkcom will face off against the Democratic nominee, Jamie Ager, in the November
title: Republicans name candidate to replace Chuck Edwards after sexual harassment investigation

author: Benita Kolovos and Nino Bucci
description:
Premier Ben Carroll promises if re-elected to ‘close every loophole’ used by high-profile accused and convicted criminals to hide their identities in the courts

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The use of suppression orders by convicted rapists will be banned in Victoria, premier Ben Carroll has announced, with his government committed to “closing every loophole” accused people currently “abuse and exploit” to hide their identities in
title: Victoria to ban suppression orders for rapists following Ralph Carr, Tom Silvagni convictions under new pledge

author: Maanvi Singh and agencies
description:
Company also announced a paid service for early access to president’s posts on policies to the social media site

Donald Trump’s media company – which owns the Truth Social platform favored by the US president – posted a $238m loss in the second quarter.

Trump Media & Technology on Monday reported that losses in the three months through June came as the company branched into new ventures including crypto. The company’s new chief executive, Kevin McGurn, announced at a conference call about the earnings that after a yearlong effort to expand into online betting and crypto, the company would be refocusing on social media.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s media company, which also owns Truth Social, reports $238m loss
